# researchPrime

**One sentence:** A careful research engine that checks claims against real evidence and tells you how solid each finding is — not just what sounds right.

## Use this when
- You need a serious investigation, not a quick web skim
- Stakes are high (a decision, a paper, a product bet) and “sounds plausible” is not enough
- You want an honest ladder of confidence: observed, corroborated, claimed, unverified, or refuted

## Do not use this when
- You only need a fast factual lookup or a short summary
- You’re looking for brainstorming or creative pivots (use Jumper)
- You need a build plan or code written (use Crucible → Foreman)

## What you get
- A structured research report at three levels (full, executive, agent-ready)
- Evidence weighted by how it was checked, with honesty stamps when checks didn’t fully run
- Multi-round adversarial review when the host can run the Node engine; a clearly labeled lighter pass otherwise

## What it is not
- Not a flattering “agree with the user” brief
- Not a code builder or product planner
- Not a guarantee of perfect truth — it reports what was verified and what wasn’t

## How to start (human)
1. Open researchPrime in Skill Foundry (or ask the agent for a deep research run).
2. State the question and what a wrong answer would cost you.
3. Approve the research plan when you’re shown it (edit or abort if needed).
4. Read the deliverable’s confidence labels before you act on any claim.

## Limits (honest)
- Full adversarial verification needs Node available; without it you still get a usable report, stamped that deep verification did not run
- It refuses to treat popularity as proof
- Long runs take real time; plan for progress updates, not instant answers

## For agents / engines
Full protocol and wiring live in `SKILL.md` next to this file (trio monorepo: `C:\dev\trio\researchPrime\`). Load that only when running the skill — this card is for people.

Emit the stakes vector + foresight receipt as the Phase-1 hand-off; the governor projects the vector to a tier that scales Phase-3. Freeze the plan and STOP.

# Poincaré knowledge maps for Foundry skills (concept, corrected 2026-10-03)

**Correction (John, 2026-10-03):** the "Piaget hierarchy" he remembered is the **Poincaré** (hyperbolic) geometry of
Nickel & Kiela 2017 ("Poincaré Embeddings for Learning Hierarchical Representations": 2–5 hyperbolic dimensions
matched or beat 200 Euclidean dimensions on hierarchical data); the **Lorentz** model is their 2018 follow-up for
stable training on deeper hierarchies. Piaget keeps a role later: the sleep loop's assimilate / accommodate cycle.
Everything this effort called the "Piaget sphere" is renamed the **Poincaré knowledge map**.

## What it is
- **One map per skill** (later, per cognitive cell), of the knowledge, methods, tools, skills it commissions and
  places to look that the skill actually uses when it executes tasks.
- **Derived, not drawn:** built up and calibrated from real data: the skill's run records (which steps ran, which
  sources and files were read, which prompts and references were used), its journal and its outcomes. It grows
  with use; it is not authored by John.
- **Geometry:** each node is a point in hyperbolic space. Distance from the origin = generality (general,
  heavily-used, highly-connected knowledge near the center; specific material toward the rim); siblings sit close;
  distant branches sit far apart. Trees embed in hyperbolic space with low distortion in very few dimensions, which
  is why it is efficient. Train and store in the **Lorentz** model (numerically stable); project to the **Poincaré
  disk/ball** for display.
- **What it is for: context management.** When the skill takes a task, a router (mixture-of-experts style) picks
  the relevant branches and pulls only that part of the knowledge base into the context window, leaving the rest
  untouched. A more general node brings a summary; descending a branch brings specifics. Over time the map makes
  the skill cheaper and more accurate because it loads less and loads the right things.
- **How it learns (Piaget's later role):** each run is assimilated (usage counts, co-use edges, outcome credit on the
  nodes used); the sleep cycle accommodates (re-embeds, splits an overloaded node, merges duplicates, moves a node
  that keeps being used with another branch), proposing structural changes for John's approval.

resources.title: What researchPrime is for
resources.summary: Investigate a difficult question, compare the evidence, and explain what is known and what remains uncertain.

resources.title: Human guide
resources.summary: When to use researchPrime and what a research answer should contain.

resources.title: Scope and research plan
resources.summary: State the question, competing branches, baselines, stakes and what would falsify an answer.

resources.title: Reusable plan input shape
resources.summary: The actual objective, axis, branches, baselines and stakes fields accepted by the planning program.

resources.title: Look ahead before gathering
resources.summary: Name a dropped or reordered branch and its counterfactual cost.

resources.title: Approve, edit or abort
resources.summary: Scope and plan are separately approved and hash bound; editing callbacks belong to the caller.

resources.title: Fresh execution boundary
resources.summary: Execution uses only the frozen plan; real isolation requires evidence and otherwise stays approximated.

resources.title: Evidence ladder and ledger
resources.summary: Observed evidence needs execution; popularity alone is not verification. This is session work described by the instructions.

resources.title: Independent origins
resources.summary: Use the shared independence machinery; agreement and independent provenance are different measures.

resources.title: Round inputs and checkpoints
resources.summary: Actual review input fields, result files and the resume protocol used by the runner.

resources.title: Verification reviewer prompt
resources.summary: Read the actual artifact; identify disputed claims and return structured findings.

resources.title: Reviewer roster and agreement
resources.summary: The imported Skeptic, Contrarian and Analyst roster, plus the code that tallies agreement.

resources.title: Select validation stakes
resources.summary: Impact, reversibility and blast radius determine the stakes tier.

resources.title: Select a locked round budget
resources.summary: Formal rounds require the triage lock before CLI or environment overrides are considered.

resources.title: Depth bands
resources.summary: The researchPrime mapping sets FULL to 8 rounds, LITE to 2 and SPIKE to 4. Its includeAdjudication knob only tightens debate in the actual runner; model quality is resolved separately.

resources.title: Stakes governor
resources.summary: Low stakes skip judge, synthesis and debate; zero on-topic findings skip that layer at every tier.

resources.title: Dry and clean stopping rules
resources.summary: The tracker uses distinct counters for a nonempty round with no new blockers and a genuinely empty round.

resources.title: Preregistered thresholds
resources.summary: Human-locked defaults, not evidence that any particular run used those defaults.

resources.title: Selected subscription families
resources.summary: Resolve valid primary settings, then the mirror only if the primary is absent. Requested families are not observed participation.

resources.title: Latest model and highest supported effort
resources.summary: Select from the provider capability catalog and upgrade links, using that model’s highest supported effort. Ambiguous ranking fails; selection begins model_attested:false.

resources.title: Provider-specific launch arguments
resources.summary: The shared policy resolver and launch argument adapter keep provider model and effort selection distinct from research depth. These are requested values, not a served-model receipt.

resources.title: Look into a silent reviewer
resources.summary: Heartbeat supervision distinguishes a productive seat from a silent or failed one.

resources.title: Engine output and report shapes
resources.summary: The engine JSON is distinct from the full, executive and agent reports the session must produce.

resources.title: Crucible: reused validation machinery
resources.summary: researchPrime imports review tally, judge and synthesis from Crucible; it does not run a whole Crucible plan.

resources.title: Foreman: reused support
resources.summary: Shared HALT and support symbols are imported; a research run is not a Foreman build.

resources.title: Gandalf: separate advisory read
resources.summary: A follow-on advisory skill, not a model automatically dispatched by the researchPrime runner.

resources.title: Literature-Review: composes researchPrime
resources.summary: A literature-specific skill that reuses researchPrime; the dependency points into researchPrime.

resources.title: Map design source references

resources.title: Poincaré concept and qualifications

resources.title: Page plan v1.1-candidate
resources.summary: Preserved source proposal: hierarchy, source cards, outline and display seams.

resources.title: Interim reporting
resources.summary: Round JSON is program output; scheduled human summaries are the operating session’s duty.

resources.title: Human feedback and reserved decisions
resources.summary: Plan edits precede execution. Reserved threshold, lineage and North Star changes require a human decision.

nodes.title: Latest model and highest supported effort

knowledge.frequency_policy: Unknown until unique recorded runs explicitly name resource ids. No title or journal count is a resource-use count.

steps.title: A question arrives
steps.summary: The session receives the research question and begins Step 0; there is no single automated question-to-report entry.

steps.title: First program call: import probe
steps.summary: The session imports contract.mjs and calls runImportSpike. GO selects engine validation; absent Node or NO-GO selects degraded prose.

steps.title: Write the plan inputs
steps.summary: The session states the question, falsifier, branches, stakes and foresight. This writing is not an engine-spawned planning swarm.

steps.title: Approve the plan without Node
steps.summary: The session records APPROVE, EDIT or ABORT in the transcript. The plan is explicitly not hash bound. This route does not call the Node planning program.

steps.title: Planning program entry
steps.summary: plan-gate.mjs reads planInputs.json, creates the run directory and invokes runPlanReviewGate; it derives a governor contract before the two-gate machine.

steps.title: Scope: approve, edit or abort
steps.summary: Gate 1 invokes intake. Approval locks depth; edits revisit scope; abort and edit overflow halt.

steps.title: Revise scope
steps.summary: The program calls onEditedScope only when supplied, then repeats intake; the ordinary CLI does not supply editing callbacks.

steps.title: Build the plan artifact
steps.summary: buildResearchPlan deterministically projects frozen inputs into the plan with stakes and foresight. It does not ask a model to invent branches.

steps.title: Plan: approve, edit or abort
steps.summary: Gate 2 writes a plan keyed by its hash and asks for approval. On approval, governance and gate records bind that plan.

steps.title: Revise and rehash the plan
steps.summary: The program calls onEditedPlan only if provided, then repeats Gate 2. The session owns meaningful content revision.

steps.title: Noninteractive approval path
steps.summary: A valid non-TTY approval provider replaces both prompts with APPROVE. This is a provider grant, not a fresh human click.

steps.title: Fresh execution context
steps.summary: The executor reads only the approved frozen plan. Real isolation needs the nonce evidence; otherwise the session stamps approximated isolation.

steps.title: Gather and grade evidence
steps.summary: The execution session searches, runs necessary experiments and writes the ledger. run-rounds does not implement this research-gathering phase.

steps.title: Validation program entry
steps.summary: runRounds first loads governance through loadGate, then reads round inputs and enforces field laws. Both CLIs must use the same run directory.

steps.title: Resolve the locked round budget
steps.summary: Formal validation requires a locked triage extension. After that lock: explicit maxRounds, then environment, then locked knobs; missing formal knobs halt.

steps.title: Resolve live or replay seats
steps.summary: LIVE_ROUND builds a prefs-aware routed agent. Otherwise injected or recorded adjudications are used. Requested family labels do not attest returned participation.

steps.title: Which review source?
steps.summary: Spawn enabled plus vacant reviews enters sidecar-or-live-panel handling. With spawning off, or nonvacant supplied reviews, use the supplied input.

steps.title: Reuse a saved reviewer sidecar
steps.summary: A valid sidecar normalizes saved reviews without paying the panel again. Malformed or zero-survivor sidecars halt.

steps.title: Resolve the reviewed artifact
steps.summary: Fresh panel dispatch needs a resolvable absolute artifact path. The helper resolves a relative artifact against runDir; path-suffixed input fields have stricter field laws.

steps.title: Independent verification reviewers
steps.summary: Dispatch the imported Skeptic, Contrarian and Analyst roster. The roster bounds three logical jobs; serial mode is available. This does not prove a three-process bound across retries and respawns.

swarm.limitation: The panel omits strictAbortJoin and its callback does not forward a cancellation signal. A respawn may overlap an abandoned call; no global subprocess cap is established here.

steps.title: Look in, retry or abstain
steps.summary: Heartbeat supervision looks into silence and permits one supervised respawn. The panel does not opt into abort-and-join, so abandonment is not proof that the old process was killed. Failed or unparseable seats abstain; zero surviving panel seats halt.

steps.title: Use supplied reviewer findings
steps.summary: Nonvacant supplied findings bypass fresh panel spawning. This is replay or operator-supplied evidence, not proof that a new independent review ran.

steps.title: Apply stakes and relevance
steps.summary: The governor tallies findings first. Low stakes exclude judge, synthesis and debate; a zero on-topic finding round skips that layer at every tier.

steps.title: Agreement, origins and conflicts
steps.summary: Agreement tallies qualifying blockers. Independent-origin quorum and default-inert fusion are recorded separately; quorum does not itself halt the loop.

steps.title: Debate conflicting origins when admitted
steps.summary: Debate fires only for conflicting attested lineages and an admitted debate layer. Concurrent conflict dispatch has no general numerical cap in this function.

swarm.limitation: No general conflict concurrency cap; Gemini-only semaphore is a different bound.

steps.title: Dispatch judge and synthesizer together
steps.summary: After any debate, both roles are launched from the same tally. Neither waits for the other; Promise.all joins both returns.

steps.title: Judge returns a verdict
steps.summary: The context-free judge reads findings. The result is recorded; the runner stops on tracker convergence rather than the judge’s verdict.

steps.title: Synthesizer returns a direction
steps.summary: The synthesizer runs alongside the judge and returns a separate direction. The next panel focus still comes from operator input.

steps.title: Await both adjudication results
steps.summary: Promise.all awaits judgeVerdict and direction before the round returns to the runner.

steps.title: Park work outside the critical path
steps.summary: New blockers can trigger the critical-path model check, including at low stakes. Parked ids leave the carried set; failure is logged and is nonfatal.

steps.title: Write the interim round result
steps.summary: Write findings, policy, judge verdict, direction, parked items and tracker state into round-N-result.json. Session summaries are separate.

steps.title: Check the actual stopping rule
steps.summary: Tracker convergence breaks the loop. Otherwise use the next existing input within the cap; exhausted inputs end this invocation. Nonempty dry and empty clean rounds are distinct.

steps.title: Correct before the next review
steps.summary: The operator fixes blockers, writes the next input and reruns. Saved round inputs are replayed from the start; adjudication may be paid again in live mode.

steps.title: Assess suspiciously fast dryness
steps.summary: After the input loop, on converged and nonconverged paths, the honesty guard evaluates fast dryness and unresolved serious findings. It adds no corrective round; its mitigation field is a stamp, not evidence of an extra probe call.

steps.title: Assemble and check engine JSON
steps.summary: Only convergence assembles, checks and writes DELIVERABLE-ENGINE.json. Conformance failure halts rather than shipping that JSON.

steps.title: Stop without convergence
steps.summary: Exhausted inputs or a round cap retain RUN-STATE.json with open blockers. No new DELIVERABLE-ENGINE.json is written on this path; an older file is not fresh evidence.

steps.title: HALT with the available reason
steps.summary: Missing approval, unlocked budget, field violations, routing errors, invalid sidecars, zero survivors or conformance failure stop work. Several runner paths write HALT-RECORD.json; not every error has an identical record.

steps.title: Write the research reports
steps.summary: The session produces the full, executive and agent versions from the ledger. The validation CLI only writes engine records; producing a file is not human acceptance.

steps.title: Retain run evidence
steps.summary: Converged and nonconverged paths both write RUN-STATE.json and a best-effort machine training record outside tests. The human usage entry is a separate instruction.

steps.title: Report ready for human review
steps.summary: Reports and engine evidence are ready to review; technical convergence does not accept or close the human product.

steps.title: Degraded prose validation
steps.summary: Without the usable engine, perform sequential review and separate judgement, with the explicit unverified-engine stamp and cross_model:false.

steps.title: Scheduled human progress summaries
steps.summary: The session arms the documented cadence at launch and relays meaningful progress. The runner’s console logs alone do not deliver chat or cockpit updates.

disagreements.title: Judge verdict does not stop the loop
disagreements.fact: Instructions call the judge the decision-maker; the actual loop breaks on tracker convergence and only stores judgeVerdict.

disagreements.title: Direction is not automatically fed forward
disagreements.fact: Instructions describe active steering. The runner stores direction, but panel focus is inp.focus supplied by the operator.

disagreements.title: Report prose is session work
disagreements.fact: Instructions promise three report levels. The CLI writes the engine JSON; its conformance check renders shapes internally rather than saving three report files.

disagreements.title: Provider grants differ from a new human approval
disagreements.fact: Instructions require explicit human approval. The optional provider path auto-approves after authorization; ordinary CLI prompts are a separate route.

disagreements.title: Same-family routing is explicitly admitted
disagreements.fact: Older prose says never self-review; the live builder admits equal saved families and requires honest single-family stamping.

disagreements.title: Conflict debate fan-out has no general cap
disagreements.fact: The panel roster is bounded. The debate function concurrently dispatches all conflicts unless serial mode is selected; the live-agent semaphore gates Gemini only.

disagreements.title: Fast-dry defaults differ from preregistration
disagreements.fact: Formal governor fallbacks use K=4 and M=2, while preregistration has K=2 and M=0. A run lock may override the fallbacks; this map does not invent that lock.

disagreements.title: Independent origins are recorded, not enforced as a stop
disagreements.fact: Round orchestration calculates quorum and debate resolutions; it returns both with the original tally. The runner continues according to the convergence tracker.

disagreements.title: A surviving panel is not necessarily a full panel
disagreements.fact: Zero survivors halt, but a partial panel proceeds and is marked degraded. Its agreement tally may yield no new blockers; the map does not equate that with strong verification.

disagreements.title: Supplied empty findings can re-fire the panel
disagreements.fact: Vacancy includes supplied reviewers whose finding arrays are all empty, not only a missing reviews array. A loaded sidecar bypasses that check.

disagreements.title: Reruns replay inputs from round one
disagreements.fact: Durable files preserve work but do not skip earlier adjudications automatically. Only reviewer sidecars avoid that panel spend.

disagreements.title: Low stakes can still call the critical-path model
disagreements.fact: The low-tier governor excludes judge, synthesizer and debate; a new blocker still reaches the runner’s separate RC-6 model call.

disagreements.title: Artifact resolution is broader than the recipe
disagreements.fact: The recipe asks for an absolute artifact. resolveRoundArtifact also joins a relative artifact to runDir; path-suffixed input fields still enforce absoluteness.

disagreements.title: Gathering, ledger and context isolation are not in the validator CLI
disagreements.fact: These are explicit session instructions. The CLI starts from approved governance and existing review inputs; this display does not pretend it gathers or proves isolation.

disagreements.title: Requested judge family is distinct from the role stamp
disagreements.fact: orchestrateRound calls makeJudge without passing model routes into that factory. The routed agent can use saved preferences, but the default role stamp alone cannot attest the served family.

disagreements.title: A skipped off-topic round can be counted dry
disagreements.fact: The governor returns a skipped tally; the runner still observes it with the same dry/empty tracker. Relevance skip does not itself suppress convergence counting.

disagreements.title: Parking changes carried blocker identity
disagreements.fact: The runner deletes parked ids from the prior blocker set. A later appearance can therefore count as new instead of carried.

disagreements.title: The honesty assessment does not dispatch a probe
disagreements.fact: The instructions describe probe-or-dissent. The assessment returns suspicious/fired/mitigated fields; the runner stores them without dispatching an extra probe. A mitigated:true field is not evidence that mitigation ran.

disagreements.title: Reviewer respawn does not prove cancellation
disagreements.fact: Instructions promise kill then respawn. The actual panel omits strictAbortJoin and does not forward its cancellation signal. The supervisor’s default false path can abandon an unsettled promise and start its replacement; three roster jobs are not a verified three-process cap.

disagreements.title: The depth knob only tightens debate
disagreements.fact: The mapping calls the knob includeAdjudication. In the governed-round call the runner supplies it as includeDebate; judge and synthesis still follow stakes even when that knob is false.

disagreements.title: Reviewer lineage can come from environment labels
disagreements.fact: The live seats resolve durable family preferences, while runRounds takes the panel lineage from REVIEW_FAMILY/ANCHOR_REVIEW_FAMILY. Actual session receipts are needed to establish service.

threshold_defaults.qualification: Default only; a particular run needs its actual governance lock.
